la:noun:macies.html:
măcĭes, ēi, f.
maceo
,
leanness, thinness, meagreness (class.).
Lit.
Of living beings and the parts of their bodies: profectus est (ad bellum) Hirtius consul: at quā imbecillitate? quā macie?; : hoc maciem facit,: reducere ad maciem,: equi macie corrupti, * : corpus macie extabuit, Cic. poët. Tusc. 3, 12, 26: turpis macies decentes Occupet malas,: tenet ora profanae Foeda situ macies, : macies aegri veteris,; .—
Of inanim, things: macies soli,poorness, barrenness,: lapidosa aurosi pulveris,: jejuna corticis,; so, corticis,: seges macie deficit,.—
Transf., of water, diminution: aquarum, e. g. at the ebb,.— *
Trop., meagreness, poverty of language, .

la:adj:mactus.html:
mactus, a, um, adj.
root μακ, in μάκαρ, blessed; cf. μακρός
.
In relig. lang., of the gods, glorified, worshipped, honored, adored (only in the voc. macte, and rarely in the nom.): Juppiter te bonas preces precor, uti sies volens propitius mihi liberisque meis, mactus hoc fercto. Jove pater, macte vino inferio esto, and 3; cf. ; for which: mactus hoc vino inferio esto,: macte hoc porco piaculo immolando esto,: macte hisce suovitaurilibus lactentibus immolandis esto, sq.: macte hac dape esto,.—
Transf., beyond the relig. sphere, with or without esto, as an exclamation of applause or congratulation: macte, macte virtute (esto), macti virtute este, etc.; and as a standing formula, macte, even with acc. (v. infra), Engl. good luck! hail to thee! etc.; in responses, bravo! well done! that's right! go on! tantumne ab re tua est oti tibi, ut etiam Oratorem legas? Macte virtute! increase in, go on in, ; : macte virtute esto sanguinolentis et ex acie redeuntibus dicitur,: macte virtute esto,: macte novā virtute, puer; sic itur ad astra!: macte virtute diligentiāque esto,: macte virtute simulque his versibus esto, Lucil. ap. : macte animo,; cf.: macte bonis animi,: macte toris,: macte hac gloriā,: macte uterque ingenti in rempublicam merito,: macte esto taedis, o Hymenaee, tuis,.—In plur.: macti virtute milites Romani este,: macti ingenio este,: vos macti virtute estote,: juberem macte virtute esse, si pro meā patriā ista virtus staret,.—With acc.: macte fortissimam et meo judicio beatissimam in ipsis malis civitatem!.—
With gen. (poet.): macte animi,; ; .—With abl.: macte animo, juvenis,.—
Absol.: Macte!that's right! well done! good!

senses: be blessed for your courage, well done

la:adj:maculosus.html:
măcŭlōsus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
full of spots, spotted, speckled, dappled, mottled, variegated.
Lit.
In gen. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): maculosae tegmine lyncis,: color,: marmor,: luna,: corium,variegated, striped,.—
In partic., in a bad sense, spotted, blotted, stained, defiled: vestis Pompeii non multa, eaque maculosa,: maculosae sanguine harenae,: litora suffusas quod habet maculosa lituras,. —
Trop., defiled, polluted, filthy: senatores,in bad repute,: maculosas commodat aedes,: vir omni dedecore,: avaritia et libidine foedus ac maculosus,: adulescentia,: nefas,unnatural, abominable,.— * Comp.: maculosiora quam nutricis pallium, Mai.

senses: war machine, military engine, siege engine
la:noun:machina.html:
māchĭna, ae, f. = μηχανή,
a machine, i. e. any artificial contrivance for performing work, an engine, fabric, frame, scaffolding, staging, easel, warlike engine, military machine, etc.
Lit.
In gen.: moles et machina mundi,: omnes illae columnae machinā appositā dejectae sunt,: torquet nunc lapidem, nunc ingens machina tignum,: trahuntque siccas machinae carinas,: frumentaria,.—
Esp.,
A platform on which slaves were exposed for sale: amicam de machinis emere,.—
A painter's easel, .—
A scaffold for building: de machinā cadere,; .—
A military machine, warlike engine: machinis omnium generum expugnare oppidum,: aut haec in nostros fabricata est machina muros,: murales,: arietaria,.—
Trop., a device, plan, contrivance; esp. a trick, artifice, stratagem: at nunc disturba quas statuisti machinas,i. e. abandon your schemes,: totam hanc legem ad illius opes evertendas tamquam machinam comparari,: omnes ad amplificandam orationem quasi machinae, * : dolum aut machinam commoliar, Caecil. ap. : quantas moveo machinas!: aliquam machinabor machinam, Unde aurum efficiam,.

la:verb:macto.html:
macto, āvi, ātum, 1 (old form of
perf. subj. mactassint, Enn., Afran., and Pompon. ap. ), v. freq. a.
macto, kindr. to Sanscr. makh, mah; intens. māmahyata, to slaughter, sacrifice; maha, victim; the ct in macto like vectum from veho; hence
,
Within the religious sphere, to offer, sacrifice, immolate any thing in honor of the gods: ferctum Jovi moveto et mactato sic,; so § 4: pultem dis mactat, Varr. ap. : nigras pecudes,: lectas de more bidentes Cereri,; Varr. ap. : mactatus vitulus concidit propter aras,: manibus divis mactata,: mactata veniet lenior hostia,: mactata Polyxena,: trecenti ex dediticiis hostiarum more mactati,: vite caper morsa Bacchi mactandus ad aras,: suovetaurilia mactanda, Fronto de Fer. Als. 3 Mai.: se Orco,: hostium legiones Telluri ac diis Manibus mactandas dabo,; cf.: ruptores pacis ultioni et gloriae,.—
Beyond the relig. sphere.
To present, reward, honor with any thing good or bad: Livius inde redit magno mactatu' triumpho, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 302 Vahl.): eos ferunt laudibus et mactant honoribus,heap honors on, extol, (also ap. ); ; .—
Far more freq. in a bad sense, to afflict, trouble, punish with any thing: illum di deaeque magno mactassint malo, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 377 Vahl.); ; ; cf. without abl., : dotatae mactant et malo et damno viros,; cf.: mactare malo adficere significat,: aliquem infortunio,: faxo tali eum mactatum, atque hic est, infortunio, * : hostes patriae aeternis suppliciis vivos mortuosque mactabis,pursue, punish,; cf.: divisores omnium tribuum domi ipse suae crudelissima morte mactaret,: aliquem summo supplicio,: aliquem morte,: mactantur comminus uno exitio,.—
To kill, slaughter, put to death: hic mactat Ladona, Pheretaque Demodocumque,: illigatas mollibus damas plagis,: haec dextra Lernam taetra mactata excetra Pacavit, Cic. poët. Tusc. 2, 9, 22.—
To magnify; trop, to extol, glorify, honor; esp. to glorify

honor a deity with sacrifices, to worship: Liberum patrem fanorum consecratione mactatis,: puerorum extis deos manes mactare,.—

Poet., to give splendor to a festival: lacte Latinas, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 11, 18.—
Aliquem or aliquid, to overthrow, ruin, destroy, : quorum ego furori nisi cessissem, in Catilinae busto vobis ducibus mactatus essem,should have been sacrificed,: perfidos et ruptores pacis ultioni et gloriae mactandos,to offer up, immolate,: cum videant jus civitatis illo supplicio esse mactatum,: aut naves uram, aut castra mactabo, to destroy, Att. ap. .—Hence, mactus, a, um, Part., sync. for mactatus: boves mactae, (better referred to maco, q. v.).

la:verb:maculo.html:
măcŭlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
1. macula
,
to make spotted, to spot, speckle, variegate.
Lit.
In gen. (only poet.), to stain, tinge, dye: telas maculare ostro,: et multo maculatum murice tigrim,.—
In partic., to spot, stain, defile, pollute: maculari corpus maculis luridis,: solum sanguine,; cf.: terram tabo,: dextra maculata cruore, Ov. de Nuce, 157.—
Trop. (acc. to I. B.), to defile, dishonor, disgrace, etc. (freq. in Cic.): rex ille optimi regis caede maculatus,; cf.: partus suos parricidio,: nemora nefario stupro,: Catonis splendorem,: tuum maculavi crimine nomen,: inde metus maculat poenarum praemia vitae,spoils,: obsoleta quoque (verba) et maculantia ex sordidiore vulgi usu ponit,.—Hence, măcŭ-lātim, adv., in a spotted or mottled fashion (late Lat.), .

la:noun:macula.html:
măcŭla, ae, f.
for malocula, malcula, dim.; cf. Sanscr. mala, dirt
,
a spot, mark, stain (class.).
Lit.
In gen., : (bos) maculis insignis et albo,i. e. with white spots,: maculis albis equus,: maculis auro squalentibus ardens (rex apum),: in ipsis quasi maculis (terra), ubi habitatur, in those spots, i. e. small places, : parcit cognatis maculis similis fera,; cf. 5, 104.—
Transf., a mesh in a net, a hole in network or in a web: rete grandibus maculis,; : reticulum minutis maculis,: retia maculis distincta,. —Of the meshes of a spider's web, .—
In partic., a spot, stain, blot, blemish, mole, etc.: maculari corpus maculis luridis,: est corporis macula, naevus,: maculas auferre de vestibus,: extrahere,: in veste facere,: e veste abluere,: mederi maculis corporis,; cf.: lentigines ac maculas e facie tollere,.—
Trop. (acc. to I. B.), ablot, stain, stigma, blemish, fault in character: quem scis scire tuas omnes maculasque notasque, Lucil. ap. : inest amoris macula huic homini in pectore,: jam ego ex corpore exigam omnis maculas maerorum tibi,: vitium commune omnium est, Quod nimium ad rem in senecta attenti sumus: hanc maculam nos decet Effugere, * : delenda vobis est illa macula, Mithridatico bello suscepta,: est hujus saeculi labes quaedam et macula, virtuti invidere,: vitae splendorem maculis aspergere,: furtorum et flagitiorum,: adulescentiae,: familiae,: in oratione nitida notabile humilius verbum et velut macula,; : ne Claudiae genti eam inustam maculam vellent,: plurima sunt nitidis maculam haesuram figentia rebus,enduring disgrace,.

la:noun:machinamentum.html:
māchĭnāmentum, i, n.
id.
,
a machine, engine; an instrument, organ (perh. not ante-Aug.; not in Cic. or Cæs.).
Lit.: machinamenta alia quatiendis muris portabant,military engines,: suspensum et nutans machinamentum,: nihil tam ignarum barbaris, quam machinamenta et astus oppugnationum,: tot genera machinamentorum ad extendendum femur,surgical instruments,: singulis articulis singula machinamenta, quibus extorqueantur, aptata,; .—*
Transf., the organs of sense, .—
Trop., a trick, device, stratagem (post-class.): callida commeantium, Cod. Th. 6, 28, 6.

Măcĕdo, ŏnis, m.,
the name of a usurer, —Hence, Măcĕ-dŏnĭānus, a, um, adj., relating to the usurer Macedo: senatusconsultum,a decree forbidding usurers to recover loans from heirs after they inherited their estates,.—

la:adj:macer.html:
măcer, cra, crum, adj.
Sanscr. root mak, to crush; Gr. μάσσω, knead; μαγεύς, baker; Germ. mager
,
lean, meagre.
Lit., of living beings (most freq. of animals): taurus, opp. pinguis,: boves,; : turdi,: mustela,: ostreae inuberes et macrae,; .—Of parts of the body: in macerrimis corporis partibus,.—Humorously of a person: valeat res ludicra si me Palma negata macrum donata reducit opimum,: nec pharetris Veneris macer est,.—
Of inanimate things, thin, poor, barren: solum exile et macrum, * : ager macrior,: macerrimi agri,: stirpes,: vineae,: libellus,meagre, thin,: ut dignus venias hederis et imagine macra,.

măchaera, ae, f., = μάχαιρα,
a sword (ante-class. and post-Aug.): machaera atque hasta, Enn. ap Fest. s. v. redhostire, p. 270 Müll. (Trag. v. 212 Müll.): succincti corda machaeris, id. ap. (Ann. v. 392 ib.): eia machaeras, (Ann. v. 585 ib.); : ni hebes machaera foret,; ; .—A weapon, in mal. part., .

la:noun:maceria.html:
mācĕrĭa, ae (post-class. form, mācĕ-rĭes, only nom. and acc., Afran. ap. ; ; ; ; ), f.
from macero, to soften; orig. a wall built of soft clay; cf. Gr. μάσσω
,
an enclosure, a wall (class.): maceriam sine calce ex caementis et silice altam pedes quinque facito,; cf. ; : quid maceria illa ait in horto, quaest quae in noctes singulas latere fit minor?: hanc in horto maceriam jube dirui,: herba in maceriis nascens,: nulla maceria, nulla casa,: post villarum macerias, Sisenn. ap. : fossam et maceriam sex in altitudinem pedum praeduxerant,; : maceria ab laeva semitae paulum exstans a fundamenta,.—
Affliction: facere illi satis vis, quanta illius mors sit maceries tibi? Afran. ap. (Com. Rel. v. 150 Rib.).

la:noun:machinatio.html:
māchĭnātĭo, ōnis, f.
machinor
,
artificial contrivance, mechanism, machinery (class.).
Lit.: cum machinatione quadam moveri aliquid videmus, ut sphaeram,: data est quibusdam bestiis machinatio quaedam, et sollertia,power of contrivance, design,.—
Transf. (abstr. pro concreto), a machine, engine: tantae altitudinis machinationes,: tanta,; 4, 17: navalis,: tale machinationis

genus, .—

Trop., a trick, device, machination, contrivance; artifice, fraud: judex tamquam machinatione aliqua tum ad severitatem, tum ad remissionem animi est contorquendus,: dolus malus est omnis calliditas, fallacia, machinatio ad circumveniendum, fallendum, decipiendum alterum adhibita,; : per machinationem obligatus,by artifice, by fraud,.

la:verb:macero.html:
mācĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
prob. from root μαγ-, μάσσω, to knead; through an adj. mācerus; v. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 395; cf. also măcer
,
to make soft or tender, to soften by steeping, to soak, steep, macerate (not in Cic. or Cæs.).
Lit.: brassicam in aquam,: salsamenta,: in piscina lupinum,: semen lacte,: (ramos genistae) marinā aquā,: (siliginem) novem diebus maceratum ... subigunt,: grana (cacaliae) in oleo,: intestina piscium sale,: podagrici crura macerantes,.—
Transf., to weaken in body or mind, to waste away, enervate.
Of the body: multos iste morbus homines macerat,; : quam lentis macerer ignibus,; cf.: Macedo siti maceratus,: pars exercitus ad utilitatem nostram macerata perductaque ad exitiabilem famem,: Fabius sic maceravit Hannibalem, ut, etc.,i. e. Hannibal's army,: muscus crura vitium situ et veterno macerat,: cor solum viscerum vitiis non maceratur,.—
Of the mind, to fret, vex, torment, distress, torture, pain (syn.: crucio, torqueo): egemet me concoquo et macero et defatigo,fret myself,: quor me excrucio? quor me macero? quor meam senectutem sollicito?; cf. : noli te macerare,: cura satis me lacrumis maceravi,: hoc me facinus miserum macerat,: infelix sollicitudo persequitur nec oratorem macerat et coquit, * : quae vos macerent desiderio,; .—Poet., with a causal object-clause: consimili ratione ab eodem saepe timore macerat invidia, ante oculos illum esse potentem,.— Mid., to vex, torment one's self: maceror interdum, quod sim tibi causa dolendi,: unum hoc maceror et doleo tibi deesse, Terenti, C. Caes. ap. Ter. fin.: ex desiderio magis magisque maceror, Afran. ap. P.

la:noun:macellum.html:
măcellum, i (măcellus, i, m., ), n.
root μαχ-; cf. Gr. μάχομαι, to fight; cf. μάχαιρα, μάχη, and mactāre; prop. butcher's stall, shambles; hence, transf.

Lit.: venio ad macellum, rogito pisces,: apud emporium atque in macello,: nostin' porticum apud macellum hac deorsum?: excandefacere annonam macelli,

; cf.: putarem annonam in macello cariorem fore,: barathrum macelli,: quae est ista laus, quae possit e macello peti?: dispositis circa macellum custodibus,: cetariorum,: ad ipsum introitum exspectare macelli,: retibus adsiduis penitus scrutante macello proxima,.—In masc.: conturbator macellus,.—Plur.: fercula nullis ornata macellis,.—*

la:verb:machinor.html:
māchĭnor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. a. [machina], to contrive skilfully, to devise, design, frame, invent (class).
In gen.: incredibile est, quantā operā machinata natura sit,: qui haec machinatus est,: haec duo musici machinati ad voluptatem sunt, versum atque cantum,: quod machiner inveniamque,; cf. —
In partic., to contrive artfully, to scheme, plot, = μηχανᾶσθαι: aliquam machinabor machinam, Unde aurum efficiam amanti erili,: aliquam astutiam corde,; ; : aliud quiddam,: inimico exitum,; cf.: sibi nefariam pestem,: necem alicui,: perniciem alicui,: pestem in aliquem,.—

(post-class.): adversus aliquem,.—Part. perf.māchĭnātus, a, um, in pass. signif.: quae (sol, luna, etc.) ni machinata versarentur,skilfully arranged, adjusted,: cum machinato strepitu tonitruum, artificial, Sall. ap. , and ap. (Hist. 2, 23, 3 Dietsch); App. de Mundo, p. 67: indicium a P. Autronio machinatum,contrived, planned, devised,: regis cura machinata fames, id. Fragm. ap. P. (Hist. 3, 34 Dietsch).

la:noun:machinator.html:
māchĭnātor, ōris, m.

Lit., of Archimedes: inventor ac machinator bellicorum tormentorum,: machinatores, qui pegmata per se surgentia excogitant,: magistri et machinatores quibus ingenium et audacia erat,: deus rerum omnium machinator fecit hominem,maker, creator,. —
Trop., a contriver, inventor: harum omnium rerum machinatores,: omnium architectus et machinator,: horum omnium scelerum improbissimus machinator,: doli,: auctor et machinator accusationis,.
